why: No standalone Libyan broadband strategy exists; this is the national instrument carrying the broadband programme, with dated initiatives to expand broadband, lay fibre and upgrade towers for 5G, assigned to named ministries and LPTIC

The only in-window act that changes broadband supply terms: the regulator and the national infrastructure operator set fibre-pair lease pricing on backbone and access networks and open FTTX on access networks to private investment, explicitly under the national telecommunications strategy

The single document dedicated to the Libyan interoperability framework; it proposes LyGIF over four phases and puts the specifications, data catalogue, central platform, API gateway and unified data dictionary in a design phase still to come, so it establishes that the framework does not yet exist

First engagement found between the identity authority and UNDP on the conceptual and operational framework for Libyan digital public infrastructure, covering governance, compliance and safeguards and the regulatory frameworks for an interconnected national system

Distinct event: the second-level LY-DNID pilot integrates directly with the LY-NDEX national data distributor and extends G2G linkage to citizen-facing verification. Repointed to the sibling slice capture of the same URL; my duplicate was withdrawn

The only binding Libyan data-localisation rule located: regulation articles 16 to 18 require storage inside Libya in approved PCI DSS data centres and flatly prohibit transferring personal, financial or credit data abroad. Sectoral, not economy-wide

The communications authority states for the first time an intention to legislate specifically for data centres and cloud computing and to issue a controls manual, and its own officials say companies currently store data without permits

The enacting statute: article 1 makes the national number the entry point to the national database and the source for identity verification before all state institutions, article 3 adds the biometrics, and articles 6 and 7 bind every public body to it. Repointed to the sibling slice capture of the same URL; my duplicate was withdrawn

The instrument the identity authority itself cites as the legal basis of electronic linkage: articles 4, 6 and 7 make it manager of the national database, bind all bodies to coordinate with it on linkage projects, and direct it to develop the National Data Exchange Network

Strongest in-window instrument on cross-government data linkage: article 3 obliges every ministry, authority and public agency to link databases and exchange information, and article 4 has the new national council adopt standards for exchanging and linking data

The adopted strategy text itself, and the authoritative statement that Libya has no AI law: pillar 2 records a legislative vacuum with no updated laws regulating the data space or codifying AI uses, and sets a four-stage legislative roadmap starting with a data protection law
Dated evidence that the National AI Charter was still a draft under public consultation five weeks before adoption, with the consultation link named

Distinct event: the move to implementation, at which sectoral guidelines for education and justice were deliberated and the development of government legislation serving digital transformation was named as a direction

Libya has no statute titled an e-commerce law; this is the instrument performing the function. Chapter 4 recognises electronic contracts and imposes fifteen pre-contract disclosures, a bar on payment for unordered goods, and ten-day return and refund rights

Decision 60 of 2026 obliging public treasuries to accept electronic payment of dues including taxes and customs, the number the existing ledger row on this decree does not carry. Repointed to the sibling slice capture; not re-staged

Distinct event: the Central Bank agrees to launch QR payment at POS from 8 March 2026, and puts figures on the acceptance layer including 170,149 POS terminals and e-wallet volumes three orders of magnitude below card volumes

The statute still governing Libyan official statistics: the Central Statistics Committee, the census mandate, article 4 confidentiality barring use of returns for tax, evidence or any other legal act, and article 5 penalties. Recorded as in force and 63 years old

Nearest thing to a binding in-window instrument: Cabinet Diwan circular 5274 affirms the identity authority original competence over national data aggregation and charges ministry information centres with entering annual reports and technical data to deadline

Distinct event: the technical readiness declaration for the population census at a meeting chaired by the Minister of Planning with the head of the Bureau of Statistics and Census. Repointed to the sibling slice capture; not re-staged

Libya has no enacted right-to-information law; this Cabinet draft is the only Libyan text found creating a request-and-appeal procedure - article 7 the right, articles 8 to 20 the timelines and appeal route, articles 26 and 27 the broad exemptions. Status draft

Disclosure act under an existing statutory duty rather than a right of access: the Audit Bureau issues its 2024 annual report under article 53 of its law and puts it on its website, covering state finances, the Central Bank and the National Oil Corporation

Distinct event: Resolution 50 of 2026 constitutes a national committee whose mandate includes a national plan to ensure equitable access to information, with a civil society access-to-information organisation seated on it, the only in-window instrument creating a Libyan body with access to information in its remit
League of Arab States signature-and-ratification table: Libya signed the Arab Convention on Combating IT Offences on 21/12/2010 and the ratification column is empty
Libya signed the UN Convention against Cybercrime at Hanoi among 60 states, delegation led by the Administrative Control Authority
GACI at the second Arab Cybersecurity Ministers Council, Riyadh 30 September 2025, committing to implement outcomes and to exchange cybersecurity legislation
CBL circular 18/2025 Article 18 absolutely prohibits transferring personal, financial or credit data outside Libya and Article 16 requires storage in approved Libyan data centres

The published national artefact closest to an interoperability standard: a six-stage method binding on government bodies, naming open machine-readable formats and required metadata fields. It carries no message schema, API contract or national data dictionary, which is the finding

Only in-window movement on a technical standard binding on all national networks: the regulator convenes the three main operators and its IPv6 committee and sets an aim of raising usage during 2026. Primary-source record of an event the base holds only via a Libya Herald report

The statute giving Libyan standards their legal force, on the justice ministry own host: article 1 creates the National Centre, article 4 makes the standards it adopts binding nationwide, and article 5 penalises breach in manufacture, services, import or export

The operative standard-setting act of the window: the supreme committee adopts the 2026 plan, a number of Libyan standards, halal meat import requirements, a GMO circulation regulation and a regulation licensing the Libyan Quality Mark

Distinct event: the twentieth Libyan-Tunisian working group on mutual recognition of conformity certificates and the quality and conformity marks, the only in-window movement on international recognition of Libyan conformity assessment
Article 14 guarantees freedom of opinion, individual and collective expression, press, publication and peaceful assembly - the founding guarantee the indicator rests on
Structured Dialogue concluded 7 June 2026 with more than 525 recommendations, 120+ members and input gathered from more than 10,400 people
A Libyan government body opened a policy document to public consultation: GIA and UNDP launched national community consultations on the Seventh NHDR

The only Libyan series carrying an identifiable communications and informatics figure: 41,157,054.743 LYD actual 2025 spending on the General Authority for Communications and affiliates, of which 5.1m development
First unified state budget in more than thirteen years adopted 11 April 2026, ending the condition that made a national digital-financing figure uncitable
Next dated observation of the same series: 2,965,391.553 LYD for January-February 2026 with nil development spending on the same body
Libya's enacted public-private partnership contracts regulation, Council of Ministers decision 507 of 2025 - the current mechanism for bringing non-state capital into public projects
EUR 11.2m EU and France instrument running 2026-2029 whose third pillar connects Libyan incubators, accelerators and MSMEs with investors
The regulator's own 2024 penetration and usage dashboard: 9,058,320 internet users, 15,436,659 mobile lines, 123,259 fixed lines, with a 2019-2024 series
First nationally representative household measurement: MICS7 interviewed 17,549 households and found 91.8 per cent with internet at home and 22.3 per cent owning a computer
The published tariff instrument itself from the operator at 40.7 per cent of the market, entry point 50 MB for 0.5 dinars a day; no ITU basket row for Libya exists after 2020
Libyana's نتواصل line for deaf and hard-of-hearing users, published prices roughly halving the unit cost for the eligible group
LTT's يومي+ unlimited-for-a-day package at 10 dinars, a new ceiling on the cost of intensive short-term access
The only named Libyan exchange object on any interconnection register, standing at 0 peers, 0 connections and 0 capacity with three allocated peering prefixes
Independent certification record for the Libyan International Telecom Company's KM-4 data centre in Tripoli, the only such record found for a Libyan national provider
A Libyan public body opening its own data centre inside the window: the Ministry of Education opened its Information and Documentation Centre data centre on 15 April 2026
NISSA's national backup policy requires geographic separation between backup storage and the organisation's own site, with tested restoration procedures and a media movement log
The only documented Libyan recovery outcome in the window: the Central Bank confirms all banking systems and services fully restored after the June 2026 cyber incident
The LyGIF interoperability roadmap writes backups in multiple geographic locations into its sustainability phase

The Libyan instrument that sets the requirement quantitatively: 99.9 per cent power availability, two separate substations, two water sources, 24 hours of on-site generator fuel and a one-week fuel contract
Most recent authoritative figures: 30 TWh generation in 2022, GECOL operational capacity 8.2 GW in 2023 from 5.8 GW, and load shedding averted that year for the first time in several
National blackout of 18 July 2026, about 1,350 MW lost after the Misrata-Khoms 400 kV line disconnected and frequency collapsed
First fire on unit one of the new South Tripoli station, 330 MW of an eventual 1,320 MW - the largest capacity milestone in the window
REAOL's own remote-areas solar programme, 400 systems totalling 310 kWp for rural clusters, border posts and pastoral wells; the World Bank rural-access series for Libya is unusable
Grid extension begun to a settlement in Omar Al-Mukhtar municipality south of Al-Bayda unserved since 1999

The Ministry of Health's own page for the Health Information and Documentation Centre, the national reference body for health statistics and health information systems; names DHIS2 as the national routine collection platform and the Civil Registry Authority cooperation on vital statistics - the institution and the system itself
National Diabetes Authority unified electronic system launched, with insulin dispensing tied to the national number and data integration between the centres and the Authority

Ministry of Health activated an integrated system connecting the ministry pharmacy department, the Medical Supply Organisation and hospital pharmacies - a distinct earlier event from the 2026-08 medical supply platform already held

The education ministry's Information and Documentation Centre states its own systems: the education data system explicitly for activating data exchange between the different bodies, the data centre, the staged SD-WAN linking ministry to schools, and GIS
Private school data completed into the education data system and a verification platform launched showing each school's linkage to the National Centre for Examinations; Decision No. 844 of 2026

GIA and the technical education ministry launched an integrated smart geographic map of 102 institutions, GIA building it and the ministry standardising the data - a ministry-to-national-authority integration distinct from the July loading

The founding act of the Civil Registry Authority, the body that maintains the source records behind every national credential, with its own legal personality, budget, branch network and transferred staff
Attorney General and the Civil Registry Authority reviewed the latest completed phase of the electronic civil registry database project and the properties guaranteeing the data's authoritativeness

Passports Authority presented a development plan for the passport issuance system including an electronic passport project and renewal of printing machines, working through the security system and the civil registry system

Article 4 of the National Number Law grants the national number from birth on the basis of civil registry data, and Article 2's 12-digit structure encodes the birth year; the operative instrument, not commentary

GIA's own service page for the electronic linkage between national bodies' systems and the national database, with its legal basis in Presidential Council Decisions 130 and 1690 of 2018 - the instrument the registry-to-identity connection runs through
LY-DNID level two pilot launched with direct identity verification, multiple authentication levels and direct integration to LY-NDEX; moves the identity layer this linkage runs into

Cabinet-level review of the civil registry system and Intilaqa, naming development of electronic linkage with the relevant bodies and data cleaning; first published statement that Intilaqa is still incomplete

The Central Bank's own description of the national rails: RTGS live 2008-04-01 for transfers between banks and public organisations, electronic clearing live 2008-08-17, corporate banking on Flex Cube, and public entities charging service fees electronically

Prime Ministerial Decision No. 60 of 2026 amends the budget and accounts regulation to oblige every ministry and authority treasury to accept approved electronic payment of dues including taxes and customs duties, with electronic receipts

CBL instruction waiving e-payment fees for the Tax Authority, Customs Authority and Libyan Ports Company and distributing 130 POS terminals in a first phase - the deployment behind the March legal enabling

The only authoritative statement of the register's actual state: paper-based administration across 39 executive administrations and 60 offices, no enterprise systems, manual registration, a six-digit sequential tax number, multiple numbers per person, and an explicitly unreliable 45,000 taxpayer count

The head of the Real Estate Registration Authority on the register's own position: eight branches, 84 service administrations, Decision No. 102 of 2011 still suspending verification, transfer and documentation, and administrative certificates issued in tens of thousands a year since 2012

Benghazi and Green Mountain branches instructed to begin mortgage cancellation, mortgaging and transfer to heirs on a legal opinion, without lifting Decision 102 - the clearest in-window restoration of registry service
Tajoura municipality and the registry office on mechanisms for inventorying municipal state property and securing the registry's official papers - the physical records the register rests on
The Libyan EMIS's own dated launch record from the operating institution: the education data system launched at school level over employees, teachers and institutions
First published operational output in the window: 136 monitorates entering data, 19,356 teachers, 498,653 students, 4,981 schools, 18,891 classes, with entry expressly still under way

Education minister opened the Centre's data centre and launched the ministry's platforms, naming the education data management system, Taysir and the Kawadir HR system, with a 100-day plan on data quality and system integration

The only systematic assessment of the delivery systems: no unified intake and registration, paper-based intake on the Family Booklet, no integrated SSF beneficiary database, and all civil registry data sharing done manually
The Social Security Fund's integrated system moved from preparing technical models to procedural operations, feeding a specification booklet for implementing companies - still pre-procurement

Quarterly grant transferred to commercial banks with the beneficiary counts published: 1,224,175 families, 3,899,482 children and 1,210,897 cards - the only current published beneficiary figures located

The prosecution service's digitisation of evidence-gathering records across six appeal court jurisdictions, with 400,000 records archived and converted to digital data - the only published volume figure for a Libyan justice information system; the Attorney General's own page could not be reached

Attorney General's office told the Human Rights Council the digital transformation system archived judicial files electronically for the first time in Libya, enabling enumeration of 108,939 convicted in absentia, 22,757 voluntary submissions, and electronic criminal record cards linked to state bodies

The only assessment of Libya's whole land-information architecture: the Survey Department created 1979, cadastral coverage about two thirds, the LSDI under the General Information Authority, datasets never unified or shared in a common format, and the 1985 destruction of the entire registry archive

Jufra municipality, State Property Authority, urban planning and the registry office preparing to enumerate state property and build an integrated database of it, and to curb possession documents issued without reference to the competent bodies

Agriculture ministry and FAO closed a national workshop supporting validation of the Agricultural Statistics Master Plan and reviewing the agricultural census questionnaire, with 32 staff trained in electronic collection and analysis

The nearest thing to a founding statement: the Ministry of Local Government's digital-transformation project director confirms the electronic correspondence system had been in official use across the ministry and its subordinate offices for over three months and was being extended to heads of municipal administrative units.
Record consolidation: the ministry assembling a comprehensive database of municipal council mayors, members and deputies, with the gaps in returns enumerated.
Service delivery: the unified citizen-service window applied in Tripoli Centre and Abu Salim with a new centre opened at Ghadames, a distinct event from the database work.

The national programme that would cover rural clinics: WHO's account of DHIS2 expansion and integration and electronic vital-statistics registration, with the foreword naming remote areas as where delivery remains hardest. National scope, explicitly, and a truncated capture.
The only in-window movement naming health facilities: four sites added in Misrata and Zliten including two primary health centres, raising the sentinel network to 15.

The national system that would cover rural schools: the education ministry's data centre opened and its education data management system, Taysir and Kawadir named, with network linkage still in progress. Baseline wins over its in-window status.

The only office-level count published: 257 civil registry offices across Libya completed matching and scanning, 1.8m households, 97 per cent. National scope; the offices are the municipal branches, so peripheral offices are inside the count without being identified.

Ben Ghalbun's review of the registry's administrations and branches and of Intilaqa's remaining obstacles - the movement is that Intilaqa is still incomplete. SHARED FILE: staged by a sibling slice for dpi.id; selected here, not restaged.

The only evidence located that Libyan police stations capture records digitally at all: the Tripoli Security Directorate system including the investigative-report system for police stations and traffic sections. Subnational, not rural; inside the window, so counted once as the baseline.
The technology hub itself, on its own page: the state technology incubator's premises, services, admission mechanism and criteria, published by the National Programme for Micro and Small Enterprises.
Capability added to an existing university innovation centre: SolidWorks 2026 licences and certified training opened to entrepreneurs and start-up owners inside and outside Gharyan University.

The enacting act itself: Decision 23 of 2025 creating the Intilaqa fund, defining a start-up, an incubator and an accelerator in Libyan law, capping seed lending at LYD 150,000 and tying the second tranche to incubator registration.
The state-linked incubator network producing a pipeline: 600-plus entries, five named ventures placed with cash prizes and incubation offers, run by the University of Benghazi incubator.

The standing published position is an absence: ITU records Libya's basic, standard and advanced ICT-skills values as NA while publishing the definitions. The first instrument that would produce a national digital-skills measure: the Qudurat assessment platform in its final stages, modelled on PIX, explicitly to generate national digital indicators.
A national-recruitment delivery channel with full operating parameters: 150 participants from across Libya, 11 August to 6 October 2026, eligibility, assessment and pass mark all stated.

The only quantified national statement of DT training reaching secondary pupils: the Ministry's own account of the Libyan Informatics Olympiad, about 4,500 pupils across all regions, 24 finalists. Baseline wins over its in-window status.
Teacher-side capacity: 100 Cyber Teachers closed at the Abu Salim education district, training secondary teachers in practical use of AI tools for content and method.

The only in-window item addressing curricular integration: Tripoli Centre's initial agreement to fold the Robo Garden platform into its education project ahead of model schools. Proposal stage, stated as such.

An institutional figure standing in for a national one that does not exist: the University of Tripoli Faculty of IT publishes 1,208 cumulative graduates with a departmental breakdown. UNESCO UIS publishes no ICT graduate count for Libya.
The largest institutional movement in the window: three ministries with the EU and Expertise France launched a National Framework for graduate employability as a single national reference.
A direct university-to-work pathway for ICT graduates specifically: a two-month placement with three bootcamps, an LYD 500 monthly stipend and stated dates.

The portal itself: Libya's operating national cross-sector citizen complaints and whistleblowing platform, run by the Administrative Control Authority under Law No. 20 of 2013, with its three channels, its forms and its selector of roughly 750 reportable state bodies.

Dates the launch of the raqeb platform to the International Anti-Corruption Day events in Tripoli attended by the prime minister and the High Council of State president, and carries the Authority's own statement of what it is for; the portal page itself is undated.

UNSMIL's own standing description of the only broad formal citizen-participation mechanism located for Libya, stating in the Mission's words that it is a consultative forum and not a decision-making body, with its membership, selection criteria and public-engagement channels.

The completion event, 7 June 2026: a final report of more than 525 recommendations, more than 120 members including persons with disabilities and youth, 35 per cent women, ideas gathered from more than 10,400 people and a youth digital platform of more than 3,200.

A distinct consultation event producing a near-final draft law, with data-protection safeguards and a National Registry among the agreed amendments - participation feeding a specific legislative text rather than a dialogue's recommendations.

The strongest Libyan official document tying a measured gender gap to access to financial and digital services: account ownership 77 per cent men against 66 per cent women, and women's financial literacy and electronic payments among the strategy's pillars.

The largest in-window addition to Libya's sex-disaggregated evidence base, publishing women's ICT use directly: 92 per cent of women aged 15-49 used a mobile phone in the preceding three months, 74 per cent the internet, 19 per cent a computer. Filed under baseline because it is the baseline for censuses-and-surveys.

A completed consultation by a Libyan authority putting women's groups into the Seventh National Human Development Report, with GIA's chairman tying women's participation to the knowledge economy and the digital transformation.

The principal Libyan disability statute in full, establishing service entitlements, the physical-access duty at Article 31 and the National Committee for the Care of Persons with Disabilities at Article 34 - and carrying no digital-access obligation, which is the finding.

The single most relevant in-window movement on digital services: the National Digital Accessibility Policy adopted by the Presidency of the Government in April 2025 moves to an implementation path with ESCWA, with mandatory compliance stated as the coming phase.

The National Charter on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, setting quantified commitments on representation and on accessible information and services - a commitment framework, not an enacted law.

The clearest Libya-specific record of a digital and biometric identity system operated for refugees: 44,223 registered in proGres and BIMS deployed in August 2020, linked by UNHCR to the design of cash and food assistance. Screened on digital identity, not displacement counts.

A completed regulatory step opening e-wallets to official foreign residents, with daily limits set at LD 50,000 and LD 100,000 - the rule that gates digital financial access for non-Libyans, with its limits stated.

The distinct implementation event five days later: Libya's first e-wallet for foreign residents and workers, registered on a passport and residency card without a bank account - the bank-account barrier removed, the documentation barrier not.

The authoritative published figure set on Libyan connectivity and the direct evidence that the divide is not measured: 98, 93 and 90 per cent mobile, 3G and 4G coverage, with every rural, urban, household and gender field reported NA.

Libya's first 5G launch, in the operator's own words - and the operator's own statement that it begins in Tripoli with other cities to follow, which is what makes it a divide event rather than a coverage event.

A completed fibre build in the south, where Libya's geographic divide sits: four further faculties connected at Wadi Al-Shatii University, with the central library and IT laboratories named for phase three.

The NSDS itself, Libya's first, prepared by the Bureau of Statistics and Census with PARIS21 and UNFPA - and the two limits that matter: no adoption decree is reproduced in it or on the Bureau's page, and its period ended in 2023.

Libya's most recent completed national survey with published results: MICS7, fieldwork August 2024 to January 2025, 17,549 households interviewed of 17,880 sampled across all 22 regions. A survey, not a census - the last completed census remains 2006.

The only located in-window census movement, and it is preparation: technical readiness confirmed at a meeting chaired by the Minister of Planning on 1 July 2026. No enumeration has been conducted and no census results published.

The published series itself: a 50-page recurring official statistical report compiled by the Central Bank's Research and Statistics Department from the administrative and balance-sheet records of Libyan banks.

An operational administrative register turned into published indicators: more than 8,000 government announcements in 2025 across 36 major public entities and more than 550 affiliated entities, with sectoral concentration and seasonality stated.

The platform itself and the institutional mechanism built to sustain it: MerWat-Libya launched 28 March 2024 with headquarters at two ministries and the Libyan Center for Remote Sensing and Space Sciences, running on FAO's WaPOR satellite data.

Libyan government ownership of a second MerWat phase, in the ministry's own record: the national stakeholders' coordination meeting for the irrigation-water-productivity decision-support platform, under the Undersecretary's patronage.

The distinct capability step: a four-day FAO technical mission training Libyan focal points in remote-sensing workflows for land-cover mapping, metadata catalogues, CKAN and GISMGR, and the AIDA system, on the MERWAT platform.

The most recent dated authoritative statement that Libya's National Meteorological Centre uses satellite data operationally, stating it twice for the August 2024 floods and recording warnings issued 48 and 72 hours ahead.

Satellite indicators placed inside national drought governance rather than research: NDVI, ESI, soil moisture, Google Earth Engine and GRACE total-water-storage anomalies named in a ten-year national strategy alongside LNMC and the remote-sensing centre.

The only in-window international project commitment naming Libya: a WMO-CIDCA-CMA trilateral MoU under which a pilot project in Libya will strengthen early-warning capability through hardware and software - an undertaking, not an installation.
